newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X Minerals jumps on Busang deal news.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X Minerals jumps on Busang deal news.

text.p: Shares in Bre-X Minerals Ltd jumped on Monday after the Canadian gold miner signed a deal to co-develop the massive Busang gold deposit.
Bre-X rose 1.05 to 25 in brisk late morning turnover of 600,000 shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Bre-X, Freeport-McMoRan Copper & Gold Inc and Indonesian interests have signed a Memorandum of Understanding for the development of Busang, Bre-X said earlier.
The venture will be 45 percent owned by Bre-X, 30 percent by two Indonesian firms and their partners, 10 percent by Indonesian government and 15 percent by Freeport McMoRan.
The Calgary-based company also announced in a separate statement that it had boosted its estimate of gold reserves at Busang by 13.6 million ounces to 70.95 million ounces.
Barrick Gold Corp was off 1.60 at 34.35 on volume of 827,000 shares after the Toronto-based gold miner said it failed to reach an agreement on Busang with Bre-X.
But analysts speculated Barrick or other mining companies eager for a piece of Busang could launch a takeover bid for Bre-X.
"Bre-X is now in play," said Dunnery Best, director of private client investing at Midland Walwyn Inc.
Vancouver-based gold miner Placer Dome Inc said on Monday it was studying whether to press ahead with its proposal to merge with Bre-X.
Last month, Placer launched a US$5.0 billion offer to merge with Bre-X in hopes of winning a share of the Busang deposit.
Placer's stock edged up 0.05 to 28.55 in modest turnover of 114,000 shares on Monday.
